title: Gas Station
description: Find the unique starting station for a circular route using the total-surplus and restart greedy insight.

data.text: There are `n` gas stations in a circle. Station `i` gives `gas[i]` fuel and costs `cost[i]` to reach station `i + 1`. Starting with an empty tank, return the index of the starting station that lets you complete the circuit, or `-1` if none exists. If a solution exists, it is unique.

**Input:** `gas = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, `cost = [3, 4, 5, 1, 2]`

**Output:** `3`

**Explanation:** From station 3 the tank never drops below zero: `4-1=3`, `+5-2=6`, `+1-3=4`, `+2-4=2`, `+3-5=0`.
Simulate the full circuit from each candidate start. O(n²), and it repeats almost identical work for adjacent starts.

data.title: Brute force O(n²)
Two facts make this linear
items: A solution exists if and only if the **total** gas is at least the total cost. If the sum of all `gas[i] - cost[i]` is negative, no starting point can work.

If you run out of fuel between start `s` and station `j`, then no station in `(s, j]` can be a valid start either — starting later only means less fuel accumulated. So you can jump the next candidate to `j + 1`.

data.title: Single pass greedy — O(n)
data.content: Track total surplus and the current run's surplus; reset the candidate start on failure.

data.title: Why skipping to i + 1 is valid
data.text: Any start between the failed start and `i` would begin with a fuel deficit that the failed start had already covered. Weakening the starting point cannot help, so those candidates can be discarded wholesale.

data.title: The uniqueness guarantee does the work
data.text: The problem guarantees a unique answer, so you can return `candidateStart` without re-simulating. If the guarantee were absent you would need to verify the candidate with a second pass.

data.caption: Running out of fuel at station i rules out every start from the current candidate through i, so the search jumps forward.
data.definition:
graph TD
    A["gas-cost nets: -2,-2,-2,3,3 total=0"] --> B["start 0: run to i=2 goes negative at -2"]
    B --> C["candidate jumps to 3"]
    C --> D["start 3: +3, +3, -2, -2, -2 never negative"]
    D --> E["total = 0 >= 0 -> return 3"]
    style E fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: The two counters do different jobs: `totalSurplus` answers 'is there any solution at all?', while `candidateStart` answers 'which one?'. Keeping them separate is what makes the logic easy to defend.
